title: Keep the cross-wagon produce/consume graph acyclic

facts.note: Task or plan text mentions wagons or their produce/consume artifacts.

Any authoring, editing or review of a plan whose wagons declare produce/consume entries. The invariant applies to the whole graph, so it fires even when the change does not touch produce/consume entries (pre-existing cycles remain violations).
SCC detector over the name-keyed producer->consumer wagon graph; a finding is any SCC containing more than one wagon, whether pre-existing or newly introduced.
Diff-level observer only used to attribute whether a cycle was introduced by this change; not a precondition for firing.

fires: A planner adds a consume entry to wagon A for an artifact name produced by wagon B, while A already (directly or transitively) feeds B by artifact name.
A planner splits a wagon and the two resulting wagons each consume an artifact name the other produces.
Two wagons have null contract fields but share produce/consume artifact names forming a loop.
A planner makes an unrelated edit (e.g. only to a contract field) in a plan whose wagon graph already contains a multi-wagon SCC: the existing cycle is still a violation.
doesNotFire: A wagon produces and consumes artifact names only internally (an SCC of size one wagon).
Cross-wagon produce/consume edges exist but form a DAG (e.g. A->B->C with no path back).
The work involves no wagons or produce/consume entries at all.

given: A plan's wagons declare produce/consume entries by artifact NAME, forming a directed graph with an edge producer-wagon -> consumer-wagon whenever a name produced by one wagon is consumed by another.
when: You author, edit or review any plan containing such wagons, whether or not your change touches produce/consume entries.
then: Ensure the name-keyed wagon graph is acyclic: no strongly-connected component may contain more than one wagon, including cycles that already existed.
prefer: Before adding an edge producer B -> consumer A (A consumes a name B produces), check by artifact name whether a path A -> B already exists; if it does, the new edge would close a cycle.
When a loop exists, restructure wagon boundaries or artifact ownership so dependencies flow one way.
avoid: Reasoning about wagon dependencies via the contract field; it is nullable corpus-wide, so edges must be keyed on the produce/consume artifact name.
Mutual or transitive produce/consume loops between two or more wagons (a consume_cycle).
Hiding a loop by nulling or renaming the contract field while the artifact names still loop.
why: A cross-wagon produce/consume cycle means no wagon in the loop can be delivered before the others; the graph must be a DAG so wagons can be ordered. Artifact names are the only reliable key because contract is nullable.
evidence: SCC analysis of the name-keyed wagon graph (nodes = wagons, edges producer -> consumer by artifact name) reports no component with more than one wagon.
verifier_detail: Nodes = wagons; directed edge producer-wagon -> consumer-wagon whenever an artifact NAME produced by one wagon is consumed by another wagon.

Run strongly-connected-component analysis; any SCC containing more than one wagon is a cross-wagon dependency cycle and a violation (term consume_cycle: a strongly-connected component of the directed wagon produce/consume graph whose size exceeds one wagon).
Key edges on produce/consume artifact name, never on the contract field (contract is nullable corpus-wide).
